title: Lugdunum
episode: Lugdunum: How Ancient Lyon Became the Capital of Roman Gaul I SLICE HISTORY
description: A documentary on how a Roman colony founded in 43 BC on the hill of Fourvière became the capital of Gaul. Its great theater, built under Augustus, still holds concerts every summer.

title: The traboules
episode: The Hidden Shortcut Passages of Lyon
description: A short look at the traboules, the hundreds of passages through courtyards and stairwells that link streets in Vieux Lyon and the Croix-Rousse. Many are open to walkers during the day.

title: The silk city
episode: EPV – Silk Weaving in Lyon | Full Documentary
description: A documentary on the silk weaving that made Lyon rich from the 1500s on, and on the few workshops still at it. The canuts’ tall-ceilinged homes on the Croix-Rousse hill were built to fit the Jacquard loom.

title: The Lumière brothers
episode: The Lumiere Brothers: Crash Course Film History #3
description: A lesson on how Auguste and Louis Lumière built the Cinématographe and held the first paid public film screening, in Paris in December 1895. Their family home in Lyon is now the Institut Lumière.

title: The first film
episode: Workers Leaving The Lumiere Factory - Lumiere Brothers 1895
description: The 46-second film the Lumière brothers shot in 1895 of workers leaving their factory in Lyon, often called the first motion picture. The factory shed where it was filmed still stands.

title: Guignol
episode: Guignol - The History of a Satirical French Puppet Show in the Backdrop of the Industrial Revolution
description: On Guignol, a hand puppet created around 1808 by Laurent Mourguet, a former silk worker, which became the voice of Lyon’s working people. The Gadagne museum has a large puppet collection.

title: Klaus Barbie on trial
episode: How the trial of Nazi war criminal Klaus Barbie shook the world | BBC Global
description: A short report on the 1987 trial of Klaus Barbie, the Gestapo chief in Lyon, for crimes against humanity. It was held in the old courthouse on the Saône and was filmed for history.

title: The Nazi hunters
episode: The Married Couple Who Caught The Nazi Butcher Of Lyon | Nazi Hunters | Timeline
description: On Serge and Beate Klarsfeld, the couple who tracked Barbie to Bolivia and campaigned for years to bring him back. In 1983 he was held at Montluc, the prison where he had once sent Jean Moulin.

title: A food capital
episode: Taking a bite out of Lyon, the French and worldwide capital of gastronomy • FRANCE 24 English
description: A report on how Lyon came by its reputation for food, from the “mères,” women cooks who ran its restaurants, to Paul Bocuse, the chef whose name is now on the city’s covered market.

title: The Festival of Lights
episode: France: Lyon's Festival of Lights dates back more than a century
description: On December 8, 1852, Lyon’s people put candles in their windows to celebrate a new statue of the Virgin on Fourvière hill. The custom grew into the Fête des Lumières, a four-day festival of light shows.
